extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A freely available benchmark dataset for language modeling designed to evaluate how well language models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles fitting Good or Featured article criteria on Wikipedia were selected, then text was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Specific sections featuring lists were removed, mathematical formulae replaced with tokens, and normalization/tokenization performed using the Moses tokenizer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Words with a count below 3 were discarded from the vocabulary and mapped to an <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Good and Featured articles from Wikipedia, totaling 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles, extracted from Wikipedia markup.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The PTB dataset has limitations including lower case tokens, stripped punctuation, and a limited 10k vocabulary, which makes it unrealistic for real language use. The WikiText dataset is sourced from Wikipedia, which may carry its own biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The PTB has a limited 10k vocabulary, lacks punctuation and casing, and has an abrupt cutoff in the word frequency distribution. Other existing datasets either have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering, which prevents learning long-term dependencies.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The WikiText dataset is intended for language modeling, particularly for improving handling of rare words and long-term dependencies. It is proposed as a replacement for the Penn Treebank in language modeling benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will make the WikiText dataset available to the community, but no specific versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described beyond the release of WikiText-2 and WikiText-103.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Words with count below 3 were discarded from vocabulary; words outside vocabulary were mapped to <unk> token; numbers were further split (e.g., 8,600 → 8 @,@ 600)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Articles filtered to Good or Featured Wikipedia criteria; text extracted via Wikipedia API; list-heavy sections removed; HTML artifacts removed; mathematical formulae replaced with <formula> tokens; normalization and tokenization performed using Moses tokenizer; for PTB: words lower-cased, numbers replaced with N, newlines replaced with <eos>, punctuation removed, vocabulary limited to top 10k words

name.evidence: we also introduce a new benchmark dataset for language modeling called WikiText

inLanguage.evidence: benchmark dataset for language modeling called WikiText

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia... The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: Following Chelba et al. (2013) a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the ⟨unk⟩ token, also a part of the vocabulary.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Extracting the raw text from Wikipedia mark-up is nontrivial due to the large number of macros in use.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The tokens in PTB are all lower case, stripped of any punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words. These limitations mean that the PTB is unrealistic for real language use, especially when far larger vocabularies with many rare words are involved.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The tokens in PTB are all lower case, stripped of any punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words... Other larger scale language modeling datasets exist. Unfortunately, they either have restrictive licensing which prevents widespread use or have randomized sentence ordering (Chelba et al., 2013) which is unrealistic for most language use and prevents the effective learning and evaluation of longer term dependencies.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We hope this new dataset can serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Hence, we constructed a language modeling dataset using text extracted from Wikipedia and will make this available to the community... providing WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 as potential options.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Following Chelba et al. (2013) a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the ⟨unk⟩token, also a part of the vocabulary.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Once extracted, specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LATEX code, were replaced with ⟨formula⟩tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer... words were lower-cased, numbers were replaced with N, newlines were replaced with ⟨eos⟩, and all other punctuation was removed.
